items.title: NAPAI Agentic AI Campus Innovation Competition
items.summary: College students across Taiwan are invited to solve real campus and field problems with Agentic AI. Entries must be operable, measurable, controllable, and field-verifiable. Online registration closes September 11, 2026; the final takes place on November 21 alongside TAAI 2026.
content: The competition is supervised by the Department of Information and Technology Education, Ministry of Education, organized by the National Agentic & Physical AI Initiative (NAPAI), and co-hosted by the Department of Computer Science and Information Engineering at National Central University and the Graduate Institute of Information Management at National Taipei University, in collaboration with TAAI 2026, the 31st International Conference on Technologies and Applications of Artificial Intelligence.

Teams tackle problems drawn from real campus and field settings using Agentic AI. Entries must be goal-oriented with task decomposition, and meet at least two of the following: tool or external system invocation, state management with dynamic adjustment, and permission and risk control. Results must be operable, measurable, controllable, and field-verifiable.

There are two tracks, a Campus Open Track where teams define their own problem and a Field-Assigned Track based on challenges published by partner organizations. Field themes cover smart academic affairs and learning support, campus administration and service workflows, library and research knowledge services, and industry and public-sector co-creation. Each team registers for one track and one theme.

All currently enrolled college and university students in Taiwan, including master's and doctoral students, are eligible regardless of major. Teams consist of 2 to 5 students, may be cross-school and cross-disciplinary, and may have one faculty advisor.

Key dates: online registration closes Friday, September 11 at 23:59; briefing and capacity-building workshop on Friday, September 18; preliminary submission deadline Friday, October 16; finalists announced Friday, November 6; final and showcase on Saturday, November 21 at The Great Roots Forestry Spa Resort in Sanxia, New Taipei City.

Total prize pool is NT$150,000. Each track awards first place NT$25,000, second place NT$15,000, third place NT$10,000, and five honorable mentions of NT$5,000 each. Rules, registration forms, field challenges, and updates are published on the competition website.
items.location: Final: The Great Roots Forestry Spa Resort, Sanxia, New Taipei City (alongside TAAI 2026)
items.eligibility: Enrolled college and university students in Taiwan, including graduate students; teams of 2 to 5
organizers: National Agentic & Physical AI Initiative (NAPAI), Ministry of Education
Department of Computer Science and Information Engineering, National Central University
Graduate Institute of Information Management, National Taipei University

items.title: 2026 AI Industry-Academia Development Forum
items.summary: Focused on Agentic AI, industrial AI adoption, innovative applications, and talent development, the forum takes place on October 2, 2026 at National Taipei University of Business, with five keynote speeches and two industry-academia roundtables.
content: As generative AI continues to evolve, artificial intelligence is moving from providing answers toward Agentic AI that understands tasks, plans workflows, coordinates tools, and executes work autonomously. The 2026 AI Industry-Academia Development Forum focuses on four themes: Agentic AI, industrial AI adoption, innovative applications, and talent development.

The morning features five keynote speeches by Yu-Chee Tseng of the Pervasive AI Research Center at National Yang Ming Chiao Tung University, Yu-Chiang Frank Wang, Director of AI Research at NVIDIA Taiwan, Chih-Yung Chang of Tamkang University, Chia-Chieh Su, Taiwan Technical Lead at eCloudvalley, and Yang-Ming Han of the Market Intelligence & Consulting Institute (MIC) at the Institute for Information Industry.

Two afternoon roundtables cover AI industry-academia collaboration and practice, and AI talent development and industrial innovation. NTPU Vice President for Research Yu-Hsien Chen speaks on AI in smart healthcare and legal practice in the first roundtable, and NTPU Vice President Yu-Shan Chang chairs the second.

The forum runs from 08:30 to 17:00 on Friday, October 2, 2026 at the International Conference Hall, 10F, Chengxi Building, National Taipei University of Business. It is organized by the Office of Research and Development at NTUB under the Ministry of Education Higher Education Sprout Project. Please refer to the official forum website for the program, speakers, and registration.
items.location: International Conference Hall, 10F, Chengxi Building, National Taipei University of Business
items.eligibility: Industry and academic professionals and anyone interested in AI industry-academia collaboration
organizers: Office of Research and Development, National Taipei University of Business

items.title: TAAI 2026 — The 31st International Conference on Technologies and Applications of Artificial Intelligence
items.summary: TAAI 2026 will be held on November 20–21, 2026, at The Great Roots Forestry Spa Resort in Sanxia, New Taipei City, under the theme “Agentic AI and Physical AI for Cross-Disciplinary Sustainable Innovation.”
content: The 31st International Conference on Technologies and Applications of Artificial Intelligence (TAAI 2026) is jointly organized by the Taiwanese Association for Artificial Intelligence (TAAI) and National Taipei University (NTPU).

The conference theme is “Agentic AI and Physical AI for Cross-Disciplinary Sustainable Innovation,” highlighting autonomous AI agents, embodied intelligence, real-world AI applications, and interdisciplinary sustainable innovation.

TAAI 2026 will take place on November 20–21, 2026, at The Great Roots Forestry Spa Resort in Sanxia, New Taipei City. The paper submission deadline is September 14, 2026; please refer to the official conference website for submission, program, and registration details.
items.location: The Great Roots Forestry Spa Resort, Sanxia, New Taipei City
items.eligibility: Researchers, practitioners, students, and anyone interested in artificial intelligence

items.title: Sea X OpenAI Hackathon APAC Series — Taiwan
items.summary: Sea and OpenAI bring their Asia-Pacific hackathon series to Taiwan for the first time, inviting teams to build AI solutions for real-life and industry scenarios.
content: Sea has teamed up with OpenAI to bring the “Sea X OpenAI Hackathon APAC Series” to Taiwan for the first time.
The event focuses on applied artificial intelligence, technological innovation, and practical problem solving, inviting participants to use AI to address real-life and industry scenarios.
For registration, competition rules, prizes, and judging, the organizers' official event page is the authoritative source.

items.title: Advanced AI Talent Cultivation Program: Agentic & Physical AI Robotics Curriculum Initiative
items.summary: NAPAI (National Agentic & Physical AI Initiative) focuses on Agentic AI and Physical AI, integrating course co-creation, faculty development, pilot courses, student competitions, and professional communities to cultivate forward-looking AI talent.
content: The Advanced AI Talent Cultivation Program centers on the Agentic & Physical AI Robotics Curriculum Initiative, focusing on the two forward-looking pillars of Agentic AI and Physical AI.

The initiative integrates seed-teacher training, co-creation of course modules, pilot demonstration courses, student hands-on competitions, and community building to strengthen AI education and practical capabilities.
The official website provides news, course resources, community activities, partners, and related learning resources. Please refer to the NAPAI website for the latest information.

items.title: AI4X Research Center officially began operations on August 1, 2026
items.summary: The university-level Advanced Research Center for Cross-Disciplinary AI is now officially operational, with its governance structure in place and first-wave initiatives under way.
content: The Advanced Research Center for Cross-Disciplinary AI (AI4X Research Center), a university-level research center of National Taipei University, has been officially operational since August 1, 2026.

The center connects research strengths in law, business, public affairs, humanities and social sciences, sustainability, and information technology. Its governance structure is in place and the first-wave initiatives are under way; the remaining research, resource, and collaboration mechanisms will be launched in phases.

Center Director: Prof. Min-Yuh Day (Professor & Director, Graduate Institute of Information Management, NTPU). Administrative window: Ms. Szu-Yin Chen, Administrative Specialist (sychen@gm.ntpu.edu.tw, ext. 66977).
organizers: AI4X Research Center, National Taipei University

items.title: AI platforms & teams already in service
items.summary: NTPU AI, the NTPU AI Assistant, and the NTPU AI Aquila Project technical R&D team are now available to the NTPU community.
content: Campus AI platforms and the student technical R&D team are now available to the NTPU community.
NTPU AI: the university AI platform, offering AI conversation, web search, campus search, and file analysis.
NTPU AI Assistant: the campus question-answering assistant, currently covering the Physical Education Office, the Center for General Education, and the Language Center.
NTPU AI Aquila Project: the technical R&D team, providing technology development, project implementation support, and education & training.
organizers: AI4X Research Center, National Taipei University

items.title: Center leadership and division heads announced
items.summary: The center director, the three division heads (Industrial Technology, Cross-Domain Application, Education & Innovation), and the administrative window are now listed on the members page.
content: The center director, the heads of the Industrial Technology, Cross-Domain Application, and Education & Innovation divisions, and the administrative window are now published on the members page.
organizers: AI4X Research Center, National Taipei University

items.title: Center mission and first-wave initiatives published
items.summary: The center's founding mission and its first-wave work items (research matchmaking, capacity mapping, data governance, and seed projects) are now published on this site.
content: The center's founding mission (cross-domain research, shared resources, industry-academia collaboration, and responsible AI) and its first-wave work items are now published on this site.

Early work includes cross-college research matchmaking, mapping of on-campus AI research capacity, a management framework for research data and computing resources, cross-domain seed research projects, faculty workshops, and a single window for external collaboration; every item carries its current status and expected timeline.
organizers: AI4X Research Center, National Taipei University

items.title: Cross-domain collaboration and research needs survey
items.summary: Faculty and research teams are invited to share collaboration interests and research needs, which will inform the first wave of matchmaking and the seed project call.
content: The center invites faculty members and research teams to share their cross-domain collaboration interests and research needs, which will inform the first wave of research matchmaking and the design of the seed project call.
Please email your name, unit, type of collaboration, and a summary of your needs to ai4x@gm.ntpu.edu.tw; see the contact page for details.
items.eligibility: NTPU faculty members and research teams
organizers: AI4X Research Center, National Taipei University
